text:
Ivan Barbashev had been stuck in a scoring slump. On Nov. 11 against Utah he got two, one of them a solo dash through the whole Mammoth team that The Athletic's Jesse Granger called an "Insane individual effort." The Golden Knights' own channel asked whether it was the goal of the year.

The season around that night is better than the goal total suggests. He has 16 points in 22 games, 12 of them assists, while playing 15.6 minutes. Vegas has taken 59.2% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, our measure of who is getting the better chances, and 8.8 points more than without him. His 4 goals on 5.2 expected goals leave a little room for more.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.2 wins above replacement last season, 42nd among 401 forwards, and worth 2.3 goals from drawing more penalties than he takes. They also note he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him on the end of the best passes, across the slot or from behind the net. The one blot this week was a roughing call after the whistle in a loss to Vancouver.
headline: Barbashev is out of his slump and still driving play
